title: KV multi-tenant interference benchmark — mixed sequence lengths and SLA heatmap
creator: Aisha Grant
description: Run a targeted load-testing harness to characterize how multi-tenant KV prefix cache interference affects tokens/sec and p95 latency across mixed sequence-length workloads. Produce a heatmap that correlates per-tenant memory cap, observed hit rate, and p95 latency under realistic interleaved traffic. Use results to set regression detection thresholds and suggest isolation or admission-control mitigations.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Synthetic harness can simulate 50 concurrent tenants with configurable hotset skew and 3-segment sequence-length mix (short/medium/long).
2) Produce per-tenant timeseries for tokens/sec, p95, hit_rate, mem_usage at 1s granularity and aggregate heatmap (mem_cap vs hit_rate vs p95).
3) Identify at least 3 workload scenarios where p95 > SLA (150ms) while global tokens/sec is within expected range.
4) Regression detector rule (alert+CI check) created with tunable thresholds and documented in Confluence.
5) Dashboard and example alarms added to Console staging with links in ticket.
test_plan:
1) Implement harness extension to generate interleaved request streams across tenant IDs with parameterized hotset Zipf alpha and sequence-length distributions.
2) Run baseline single-tenant and then incremental multi-tenant runs (10, 20, 50 tenants) under three memory cap policies (per-tenant fixed, proportional, shared capped).
3) Sweep eviction policy: LRU, segmented-LRU, and write-through-prefetch.
4) Capture detailed metrics (tokens/sec, p95, p50, p99, cache hit_rate, evictions/sec, memory RSS).
4) Annotate runs with synthetic rollout events (model weight updates) to measure warmup/coldstart interference.
5) Export heatmaps and regression digest and compare vs previous baseline run (runtime-1.18).
steps: - Develop harness knobs in kvt-harness (branch kvt/mt-heatmap). - Add tenant generator that supports per-tenant token mix and hotset drift. - Integrate with perf-collector (Prometheus metrics + push to perf DB). - Create Grafana heatmap panel and Console route for the experiment. - Run overnight sweeps on staging pool and collect artifacts. - Draft regression rules and PR to monitoring repo.
notes:
Design trade-offs: running full 50-tenant sweeps is noisy but necessary to expose interference. We may first run controlled seeded runs (deterministic RNG) to derive reproducible baselines. Cost: ~200 GPU-hours on staging over sweep matrix; propose using low-cost preemptible cluster for initial runs.
Decision log: we will focus on per-tenant memory-cap experiments before trying admission-control policies to keep scope bounded. If interference is severe, next ticket will prototype per-tenant admission control and priority routing.
initial_results_summary: Preliminary small-run (10 tenants, mixed seq lengths) results: tokens/sec stable (~120k tks/s baseline) but p95 increases nonlinearly as hit_rate drops below 0.72. Observed knee: at 0.65 hit_rate p95 rises from 95ms to 230ms for medium-seq tenants. Evictions/sec correlated with long-seq tenant bursts. These early signals validate the hypothesis that mixed seq-lengths amplify eviction interference. Full sweep scheduled 2025-02-25.
regression_detection_proposal: Alerting rule: if per-tenant p95 > 150ms AND hit_rate drop > 10% from baseline for 30s window, fire P1 regression alert. CI check: compare new sweep heatmap to baseline; fail if area of config space with p95>150ms increases by >15%. Rules and thresholds will be tuned after full-sweep data.

qa_notes: QA should validate reproducibility by running the provided deterministic seed suite and verifying that recorded heatmap coordinates are within 5% of baseline for the seeded runs. Include a sanity-check job that replays the top-3 failing scenarios and produces a flamegraph of eviction activity.
